title: 023 · Why? #11: four derivatives of sin x go round to sin x; y″ = −y, (sin 2x)″ = −4 sin 2x (predict-first, white)

captions.instagram:
NDA Maths · Differentiation. Differentiate sin x four times. You get…? A sin x · B −sin x · C cos x 👇

A. Each derivative slides the sine wave a quarter of its length to the left: sin → cos → −sin → −cos → sin.
Four quarter turns = one full turn, so you're back where you started.
Two turns flip it upside down: y″ = −y. For sin 2x each turn also doubles it, so y″ = −4y.
Traps: −sin x stops after two derivatives; cos x after one.

NDA asked it in 2019 (I), Q83: y = a cos 2x + b sin 2x gives y″ = −4y, so y″ + 4y = 0.
